##Visualizing the area

We sketch the graphs of $f$ and $g$ first.

![graph](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/da09be8f37aaa8c679562ce9e7cafbee8c572735)

From the graph, it appears that $g(x)\ge f(x)$ between $x=-6$ and $x=-2$ . From this we are looking to evaluate:

$\displaystyle \int_{-6}^{-2}\left( g(x)-f(x) \right)\,dx$

options.explanation:
Our expression simplified to $20+4\ln(6)-4\ln(2)$ , which we can write as:

$20 + 4(\ln(6)-\ln(2))$

Subtracting the logarithms of two numbers is equivalent to taking the logarithm of their quotient.  So we can write our expression as:

$20 + 4\ln\left( \dfrac{6}{2} \right) = 20 + 4\ln\left( 3\right)$

Finally, to multiply a logarithm of an argument by a value is the same as taking the logarithm of that argument raised to the power of the factor before the logarithm.  So we have: 

$20+\ln \left( 3^4 \right) = 20+\ln(81)$
